gaps.sentence: The new bypass will be ___ (BENEFIT) to thousands of commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'Be beneficial to' — the adjective follows the verb 'be'.

gaps.sentence: He answered all the questions with great ___ (CONFIDENT).
gaps.explanation: 'Great' needs a noun: confidence. 'Confident' is the adjective.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (IDENTIFY) of the body took weeks.
gaps.hint: noun: the act of establishing who
gaps.explanation: 'The identification of the body' — the process noun is required.

gaps.sentence: His ___ (BEHAVE) at school has improved enormously.
The old factory will be ___ into flats (MODERN).
gaps.hint: verb needed in the passive (-ise); past participle
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: modernise. The passive 'will be' needs the past participle 'modernised'.

gaps.sentence: This guidebook is really ___ for travellers (USE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ful means full of: useful. 'Useless' is the negative opposite.

gaps.sentence: The crowd waited ___ for the gates to open (PATIENT).
gaps.explanation: An adverb modifies the verb 'waited': patiently. 'Patients' are people in hospital.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.
